steps.text: Put the diced yam in a microwave-safe bowl; cook in the microwave until cooked through and fork-tender, stirring once, 5 to 7 minutes.

Coat the bottom of a large skillet with olive oil and place over medium heat; cook and stir the turkey until crumbled and evenly brown, 5 to 7 minutes. Stir the onion, garlic, and jalapeno pepper into the turkey and continue cooking until the onions begin to caramelize, 7 to 10 minutes. Season with the chili powder, cumin, Cajun seasoning, and salt. Pour the salsa over everything; fold the sweet potatoes into the mixture. Allow the mixture to cook until the excess moisture evaporates. Garnish with the cilantro. Serve with the warm tortillas.

raw_recipe.description: Spicy tacos with low fat turkey have a sweet-hot flavor, yams give them a surprising twist.

review.reviewBody: Delicious! Only change I made was to cut back on the jalapeños because I am a wimp. I used on pepper and it was just about right for me. I loved how the sweetness of the yam contrasted with the spices. I served this with fat free sour cream and in whole wheat tortillas

We loved these alternative tacos! I wish I would have used the 4 jalapenos as written, I got scared to use all 4 because of the reviews. But we like things hot, so 4 would have been fine. Actually, I used 2 Serrano peppers, which tend to be hotter. One without the seeds and membranes and one with them. I did add some chopped cabbage for crunch and used corn tortillas for a more authentic taste. Yum!

I really loved these tacos!
I made a few modifications: I used a 1 lb. of ground turkey, increased the spices, used 3/4 cups of the salsa verde and served it on corn tortillas that I toasted over an open flame. YUM!
I also did a version were I skipped the tortillas altogether and served this with regular salsa in addition to the tomatillo salsa over shredded lettuce as a taco salad. That was also excellent!

Tried these tonight and I agree with the 5 star rating. They are delish! It was a nice variation from the usual taco recipe. I am on a low cal/low carb healthy eating plan and these work perfect with low carb whole wheat tortillas and fat free sour cream. YUMM!

Wonderful! These were a hit with everyone, including my 4-yr-old (who likes spices). I used some canned roasted chilis and a whole serrano in place of the jalapenos, since that is what I had. I half-cooked the yam before peeling and cubing, since that makes it easier to cut. Next time, I'll dice the yam quite small to spread it out more evenly. This recipe is a real winner, healthy and delicious.

I make a variation on this recipe and it is DE-LISH. I add half a tbsp oil to the onions and cook those up a bit before adding the turkey, then I put in the second half tbsp and brown the turkey. I left off the jalapeno and cilantro because I'm not a fan. Instead of the tomatillo salsa I just added diced tomatoes - about a cup worth. I followed the recipe pretty close for the other spices - probably added a little more chili powder. Adding sour cream to the finished product cools it a little bit. Very yummy!

Five stars, for sure.

I used what I had on hand. Pictsweet frozen Brown Sugar Sweet Potatoes, cut smaller (the sweetness turned out to be a great thing! One canned chipotle pepper with adobo sauce (in lieu of chili powder), a few jarred jalapeno pepper slices, and red salsa. 

Holy smokes this was good. Seriously, I knew it was a keeper at first bite. Don't be afraid to use those glazed sweet potatoes. It's easy and tasty!

Made this tonight & added some lime juice to the mixture. I also melted in a package of goat cheese which added a delicious creamy flavour. I cooked some quinoa in chicken broth with pepper & lime juice, and served on top of the quinoa. Super yummy!

A little bit of work but well worth it!! I doubled the recipe (love leftovers) used 7 jalapeños, forgot tomatillo salsa so used regular & it was fantastic! Topped with avocado will try Greek yogurt next time. Only thing I would do differently is chop the sweet potatoes a little smaller.

This is going in the regular dinner rotation. So easy to make and so delicious. I did have to make 2 changes. I used serrano peppers instead of jalapenos so the kids would eat it but then just served fresh jalapenos on top of the adults. I also added more then a cup of salsa verde. More like 1 3/4 C. Served them up with some mexican queso fresco cheese, sour cream, shredded cabbage, and avocado. There were no leftovers and the kids are still talking about them.

You're silly not to give this recipe a try! I was looking for a recipe to use my ground chicken with and stumbled upon this. I wish I could give more than 5 stars that is how great it is!! 
I did double the recipe, but only used 1 large jalapeno because I have teenagers & small children (I didn't want it too hot for the little ones). I also added 1/2 cup of baby bella mushrooms, diced real small) because I needed to use them up. 
It was gone! Not one bit left for my husbands lunch the next day.
Very easy to make and so good. I added a little onion salt and used corn tortillas.
Great recipe! The only addition we made was adding in one can of diced green chilis.
Very good! I had to substitute a few of the seasoning and only added 2 jalapeños. It was just a medium spicy without giving you the sniffles. Great combination of the turkey and the sweet potato!
Great meal are grandkids love them first time making it this . I served it with black beans and rice and flour tortillas. I will Definitely make this again

Have made these several times with just a few tweaks. I only use 1 jalapeño, omit the cajun seasoning(since I don't ever have) and replace the cilantro with parsley(since I'm not a huge cilantro fan). We like to top with lettuce, cheese and sour cream...but I've had without and delicious both ways! My teenage kids said that these have moved near the top of the their favorite meals list!
These tacos are very flavorful. I made them as the recipe is listed and even my picky child liked them.
These are OK and I ate them but will probably not fix them again. I love to cook and try new things so thanks Fooddude.
These are very good

These are delicious. They're a little spicy for my taste so I shall cut down on the jalapenos next time or, better yet, add sour cream to my taco. I served these with Mexican White Rice from this site and a can of refried beans.
